messages:
Maya Chen: Drafted PRD skeleton for Dedicated Capacity SLA & Autoscale. Putting initial acceptance criteria + sizing heuristics. PTAL: https://paper.redwood.team/d/ded-capacity-sla-draft
Vikram Singh: Nice. Can you add customer-driven SLOs? e.g., p95 latency <= 150ms for gen endpoints, min throughput 100 rps per pool.
Maya Chen: Added p95 targets and throughput baseline. Also included failure modes and fallback (hosted fallback to smaller model).
Ellie Park: For autoscale, we need ramp rules + cooldown. Suggest: scale up when avg util > 70% for 2 mins, scale down when < 30% for 10 mins. Also cap scale rate to 2 nodes / 5 min.
Ryan Morgan: Agree. Also add cold-start penalty budget — startup GPU init takes ~45s. Acceptance criteria: 95% of scale-ups complete in <60s.
Vikram Singh: Edge case: model hot-cache invalidation during deploys. Add requirement to warm KV cache or pre-warm with synthetic prefixes.
Maya Chen: Noted. Included synthetic pre-warm job in PRD. Also draft rollback policy: if latency spike > 20% for 5 min post rollout then automatic rollback.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout to 5% of traffic at 2025-07-14T09:00Z
Ellie Park: Question on sizing: how did we pick 100 rps baseline? customers A/B had 70-120 spikes. Maybe make it workload-profile driven and include a sizing calc.
Maya Chen: I added sizing calc table + formula: required_workers = ceil((expected_peak_rps * cost_factor) / per_worker_rps). See snippet:
```
# autoscale policy (yaml)
min_workers: 2
max_workers: 50
scale_up:
  threshold: 0.7
  window_sec: 120
  max_delta_per_window: 2
scale_down:
  threshold: 0.3
  window_sec: 600
```
Ryan Morgan: Acceptance tests: synthetic load tests with model variants, verify throughput and latency SLOs under 99% of test runs. Add runbook links.
Vikram Singh: Add cost guardrails: unit tests must report token-level cost delta; if cost per token > baseline + 15% must require PM signoff.
Maya Chen: Done. I'll update PRD and request RFC review tomorrow @Ryan Morgan @Ellie Park. Any last asks?
Ellie Park: :thumbsup: looks good. One more — include SLA wording for enterprise customers (financial SLA)? maybe later.
